newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia political risk seen higher - Investec.
newsitem.headline: Zambia political risk seen higher - Investec.

text.p: South Africa's Investec Bank Ltd said on Wednesday it perceived the political risk of investing in Zambia to have increased since 1996.
It advised intending financiers in the country to insure themselves against political and commercial risk.

"First quarter 1997 risk index ratings by the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) give Zambia an EIU overall score of 70 (on a scale of 100 as maximum risk) versus South Africa at 51," said Michael Smith, head of Investec's Emerging Markets Finance Division.

"Our view is that, taking current trends and recent developments into account, we would support a further re-rating of Zambia (with the) December 1996 overall score at 80," he said at an investment opportunities conference organised by the Financial Times.
Zambia has been faced with considerable political unease following the holding of controversial general elections in November 1996.
Seven political parties boycotted the elections, condemned as unfair by the European Union, whose members cut aid to the country in protest.
Smith advised financiers to protect themselves by insuring their investment in the country.
"Banks are generally not prepared to accept relatively high levels of political risk in conjunction with the sorts of risks inherent in resource projects," he said.

"A way around this is to insure against political and commercial risks through export credit agencies or other multi-lateral agencies. The South African export credit agency has supported Investec in Zambia to date and various other agencies are open or cover for Zambia," he added.
Smith was speaking only hours after Zambian president Frederick Chiluba painted a rosy picture of political and economic stability in the country to the conference.

"Our political stability and the existence of a legal framework that protects and guarantees private investment against state appropriation make Zambia a truly tempting location for private investment," Chiluba said when he opened the two-day conference.
